description: `is_a?`'s type argument evaluates to a word that is not a recognized Core type, raising `ol-unknown-type` naming the word — the same code and params as the worded form's rule (`spec/commands.md:708`, `spec/error-model.md:127`). Issue #99. WHY stage=runtime, when `spec/error-model.md:127` registers `ol-unknown-type` as `semantic`: the PREFIX form evaluates its type argument, so the type word is not statically knowable and no checker can decide it (`spec/execution-model.md:167-169`, `spec/grammar.md:234`). The WORDED form `is a` takes a literal type word in the grammar, so it IS statically knowable and is caught at the registered stage — measured, `check()` over `print (5 is a "banana")` reports `ol-unknown-type`/`semantic`, while `check()` over this fixture's program reports nothing at all. The sibling pair pins both sides: `core-language/check/type-unknown-in-is-a` and `core-language/execution/is-a-unknown-type`. That reason is independent of issue #815, and this fixture's result is unchanged by it — measured identical at #815's parent and at the current tip. Since #815 `execute()` DOES run Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:632`, `:659-664`); here the check finds nothing, so Phase 2 begins, and execution halts at the failing statement keeping the `instruction` event asserted below. Issue #1156 corrected two false claims this description previously carried: that the stage was runtime because `execute()` did not run the checker — which #815 falsified — and a denial that this statement executed at all, which contradicted the event asserted below and was pasted from the check-caught sibling `is-a-unknown-type`, where both of its clauses are measured true.
